title: U.S. House · New York's 15th District
area: The South Bronx, including Concourse, Highbridge, Morrisania, Hunts Point, Soundview, Parkchester, Castle Hill, and Co-op City.

context.text: Incumbent Ritchie Torres won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 58.1% of the vote, defeating Jose Vega (22.2%) and Michael Blake (19.1%).
The Republican primary (Stylo A. Sapaskis) and Conservative Party primary (Gonzalo Duran) were both canceled; each candidate advanced unopposed.
John Maynard Harris, who had been listed under the 'What The H.E.C.' party line, withdrew or was disqualified and does not appear on the November 3 general-election ballot.

summary.text: Torres grew up in public housing in the Bronx and began his career as a staffer to a City Council member. He was elected to the New York City Council in 2013 at age 25 and to Congress in 2020, and has represented NY-15 since January 2021. He sits on the House Financial Services Committee and the Select Committee on Strategic Competition with the Chinese Communist Party, and has sponsored legislation on housing, immigration-detention oversight, and campaign-finance transparency.

background.text: Born in the Bronx on March 12, 1988. According to his official biography, his mother raised him, his twin brother, and his sister in a public-housing project, working minimum-wage jobs.
Graduated from Herbert H. Lehman High School in the Bronx in 2006 and attended New York University from 2006 to 2007.
Before seeking office, worked on the staff of Bronx City Council Member Jimmy Vacca and as a community organizer.

Elected to the New York City Council in 2013 at age 25, becoming the city's youngest elected official and, per his official biography, the first openly LGBTQ+ person elected to office in the Bronx. He represented District 15 until his election to Congress.

On the Council, chaired the committee overseeing the New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) and held what the biography calls the first committee hearing ever in public housing, according to his official biography; he also served as a delegate to the 2016 Democratic National Convention.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2020 to succeed Rep. José Serrano and took office in January 2021.

In the 117th Congress served on the Financial Services and Homeland Security Committees. In the 119th Congress he serves on Financial Services (subcommittees on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence; Housing and Insurance; and National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions) and the Select Committee on Strategic Competition with the Chinese Communist Party.

priorities.text: "Bronx needs one of our own to fight for us in Washington, and I'm honored to carry the mantle."

"I'm fighting for quality health care and housing, schools and jobs. I'm standing up for immigrants, seniors, and youth. I'm fighting everyday to protect our neighborhoods from gun violence and make the Bronx a safe, decent, affordable place to live."

positions.summary: In a March 2026 statement on the war in Iran, said the President cannot constitutionally wage war without congressional authorization unless the nation has been attacked or faces an imminent attack.
positions.quote: The President cannot constitutionally wage war without congressional authorization unless the nation has been attacked, is under attack, or faces an imminent attack.

positions.summary: In a March 14, 2025 statement on the Senate continuing resolution, described the budget fight as leverage to halt or impede cuts to the social safety net, particularly Medicaid.
positions.quote: The CR represents the best (and possibly only) leverage that we as Democrats will have to halt or impede Donald Trump’s systematic decimation of the social safety net—particularly Medicaid.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services (Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence; Housing and Insurance; National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions subcommittees) and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, 119th Congress.

Sponsored the Housing Temperature Safety Act of 2025 (H.R. 638), introduced January 22, 2025, which would pilot a program requiring owners of federally subsidized rental units to install heat sensors and would let housing agencies automatically issue violations against non-compliant landlords.

Sponsored the Helping More Families Save Act (H.R. 4385) with Rep. William Timmons, introduced July 14, 2025, to let HUD-assisted families build escrow savings from rising earned income without losing benefit eligibility.

Sponsored the Point-Access Housing Guidelines Act of 2025 (H.R. 6345), introduced December 1, 2025, directing HUD to issue federal guidelines for permitting point-access ('single-stair') apartment buildings.

Co-sponsored the Families Deserve to Know Act with Rep. George Latimer (NY-16), introduced August 13, 2026, which would require ICE to notify a detained person's family of a death or medical emergency in custody and to report every custody death to Congress and the public.

candidates.name: Stylo A. Sapaskis
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed after the Republican primary was canceled

summary.text: Sapaskis is a Bronx-based Republican making his second run for NY-15 after losing to Torres in 2022; he has also run for New York State Senate in 2010 and New York City Council in 2025. His campaign centers on inflation, a higher minimum wage, more police presence, and financial aid for higher education.

background.text: According to a voter-guide profile, he holds an Associate of Applied Science in Corporate Cable Communications from Borough of Manhattan Community College and a B.A. in Film Production/Cinema Studies from the City College of New York; and is pursuing an M.F.A. in the same field at the New York Institute of Technology.
Ran for New York State Senate in 2010 as the Republican nominee, unopposed in the primary, and lost the general election to Adriano Espaillat.
Ran for NY-15 in 2022, losing to Ritchie Torres 82.7%-17.2%.
Ran for New York City Council District 11 in 2025 as the Republican nominee, receiving 13.0% against incumbent Eric Dinowitz in the general election.
Became the Republican nominee for NY-15 in 2026 after the June 23 Republican primary was canceled.

priorities.text: "Under the current Democratic influences and policies, our country is suffering inflation and the raising of gas and food prices."
"As your Congressman, I purpose to elevate minimum wage to 20 dollars per hour as well as having financial aid to be offered in higher education."

positions.summary: In a 2022 candidate statement on iVoterGuide (his 2022 House run), said he would raise the minimum wage to $20 an hour.
positions.quote: As your Congressman, I purpose to elevate minimum wage to 20 dollars per hour as well as having financial aid to be offered in higher education.

candidates.researchNotes: No dedicated 2026 campaign website was located; positions above come from a candidate questionnaire response published by iVoterGuide. Sapaskis has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Gonzalo Duran
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed after the Conservative Party primary was canceled

summary.text: Duran is a Bronx-raised U.S. Marine Corps veteran and chief executive running on the Conservative Party line, and serves as vice chairman of the Bronx Conservative Party. He has run for City Council (2023), Congress (2024), and Public Advocate (2025). His 2026 campaign centers on opposing what he calls socialism, along with public safety, concerns about housing development, and government transparency in the Bronx.

background.text: Born in New York City. In a Ballotpedia survey response, he describes himself as born, raised, and educated in the Bronx.
Earned a high school diploma from DeWitt Clinton High School and a bachelor's degree from Fordham University in 2014.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 2003 to 2011. He describes reaching the rank of Sergeant and completing a tour in Iraq.

Describes himself as CEO of Devil Dog USA Inc., a district leader for the 79th Assembly District, a chaplain, and host of a veterans talk show called Vet Talk; he describes his nonprofit work as helping veterans transition back into their communities.

Vice chairman of the Bronx Conservative Party and, per his campaign materials, a district leader for the 79th Assembly District. In February 2026 he wrote that he left the Democratic Party about three years earlier and accepted the Bronx Conservative Party's endorsement for Congress.
Ran for New York City Council District 17 in 2023 on the Conservative Party line (4.2%), and for NY-15 in 2024 on the Republican and Conservative lines, losing to Torres 76.2%-21.0%.

Announced a 2025 mayoral bid in November 2024, but appeared on the November 2025 ballot as a candidate for Public Advocate, losing to Jumaane Williams with 24.5% on the Republican, Conservative, and United Alliance lines.

priorities.text: "My top priority in this race is to confront and push back against socialism."
"I have long advocated for veterans, family values, community stability, and quality of life."
"Government transparency is lacking, and residents are rightfully asking where their money is going."

candidates.researchNotes: Some platform-page material (police/housing positions) appears to originate from Duran's earlier City Council campaign but remains posted on his current 2026 campaign site. Duran has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey.

statements.quote: Housing is necessary, but reckless over development is dismantling communities, displacing families, and replacing affordable single family neighborhoods with housing many working residents cannot afford.

statements.quote: Increase the amount of NYPD and surveillance to areas with high crime rates.

statements.quote: Encourage landlords to cap rent at an affordable level. Build stronger legislation to protect residents from landlords who drastically raise the rent.

summary.text: Easton is a lifelong Bronx resident and public-school teacher running on the Party for Socialism and Liberation line in his first political campaign. He completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, describing a platform built around public housing, a $30 minimum wage, and ending U.S. military aid to Israel.

background.text: In a Ballotpedia survey response he describes himself as "an educator, father, husband, and socialist" and a lifelong Bronx resident.

Has taught in South Bronx public schools since 2012 according to the Bronx Times (13 years of teaching English there, per his own survey response); the Bronx Times describes him as a high school teacher.

His 2026 run is his first political campaign, per the Bronx Times; he is a member of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, which is running him as an independent candidate, and hosts a series of campaign events called "Class is in Session" on Bronx issues.

priorities.text: "My campaign is building a grassroots movement in the Bronx for socialism. The Bronx deserves lower rent, higher wages, clean air, free healthcare, fully funded schools, and a future that belongs to us — not the billionaires, not the landlords, but the workers who make society run."

"I will fight to repeal the Faircloth Amendment, the federal ban that's blocked new public housing construction for decades. New public housing builds will not only be good quality and fully modernized, but also truly affordable, with rents that cost us no more than 20% of our income."
"That's why, on day one, I will fight to raise the federal minimum wage to $30 an hour."
"In Congress, I will demand the bloated U.S. military budget be slashed by 90%. I will also fight to end all U.S. aid to Israel."

positions.summary: Easton calls for repealing the federal Faircloth Amendment so new public housing can be built.
positions.quote: I will fight to repeal the Faircloth Amendment, the federal ban that's blocked new public housing construction for decades.

positions.summary: Easton says new public housing should be capped at 20% of a resident's income and that housing should be removed from the private profit motive.
positions.quote: New public housing builds will not only be good quality and fully modernized, but also truly affordable, with rents that cost us no more than 20% of our income.

positions.summary: Easton would raise the federal minimum wage to $30 an hour.
positions.quote: That's why, on day one, I will fight to raise the federal minimum wage to $30 an hour.

positions.summary: Easton says he would end all U.S. military aid to Israel and cut military spending broadly.
positions.quote: I will demand the bloated U.S. military budget be slashed by 90%. I will also fight to end all U.S. aid to Israel.

candidates.name: Jose Vega
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the June 23 Democratic primary to Torres (22.2%); on the November general-election ballot on the Speak The Truth Party line

summary.text: Vega is a South Bronx political organizer affiliated with the LaRouche movement who ran unsuccessfully in the 2026 Democratic primary and appears on the general-election ballot on the Speak The Truth Party line. His platform centers on Medicare for All, reindustrializing the Bronx, immigration reform, and ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars.

background.text: Born in New York City in 1998 and raised in the South Bronx, according to his campaign website; Ballotpedia lists him as having attended Bronx Community College and worked as a barista.

Describes working with the LaRouche movement since age 16, helping organize concerts, youth choruses, and science programs for teenagers; Ballotpedia lists affiliations with the Schiller Institute and the LaRouche Organization.
Ran for NY-15 in 2024 on the LaRouche Party line, receiving 2.4% of the vote; his campaign describes that run as an independent candidacy.
Ran in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, finishing third with 5.7% behind Torres and Michael Blake, and is on the November ballot on the Speak The Truth Party line.

priorities.text: "Make the Bronx the center for reindustrialization of the United States"

positions.summary: Vega's platform calls for 'a real medicare for all policy.'
positions.quote: A real medicare for all policy

positions.summary: Vega opposes deporting long-settled immigrants and proposes residency pathways and temporary work visas instead.
positions.quote: Millions of immigrants, who have lived in this nation for perhaps as long as 50 years, are now being threatened with forced deportation

positions.summary: In a statement titled 'Reject AIPAC, and Reject War,' Vega's campaign cited calls, including from Israeli citizens, for American funding of Israel's military campaign to stop until the war ends.
positions.quote: students, young people, and even strong supporters of Israel, including Israeli citizens, have called for the war to stop, and for American funding of Israel to stop, until the war stops.

researchNotes: Federal key floor votes and FEC finance totals for Torres are populated separately by script. Minor-party candidates Sapaskis, Duran, and Vega have limited independent press coverage; their positions above rely primarily on their own campaign statements. No 2026 Candidate Connection survey responses were available from Sapaskis, Duran, or Cinquemani-adjacent sources for this race. Pass 2 (Oct. 2026): reviewed Duran's campaign platform pages (safety, housing, health, education, employment, environment, transportation, veterans), which are written in a City Council-candidate voice and mostly address local issues; one housing statement was added. No 2026 campaign-site statements found for Sapaskis; the only issue statement found for him is the 2022 iVoterGuide answer already cited. Sapaskis and Duran had not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey as of the research date (Duran completed it in 2024 and 2025). No occupation or employer was found for Sapaskis, and Easton has limited press coverage beyond a Bronx Times profile.
